findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-code credential is removed with removeStoredCredentialById, which neither targets user storage nor tolerates a null id
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns the credential from the user storage (federated) first. When `allCodesUsed()` is true for such a credential the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That method only operates on the local Keycloak DB, so the exhausted credential stays in the user storage (and `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` on the storage keep treating it as valid). Worse, federated models built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` (as in the test provider) have a null id, so the local store is queried with a null primary key (JPA `em.find` throws `IllegalArgumentException`), failing the login after a correct code was entered. For federated credentials the removal should go through `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` (or be skipped and left to the provider).

findings.title: Login form bean calls Optional.get() unconditionally; user storages that validate recovery codes without exposing them via getCredentials crash the login page
findings.body: With this PR a user storage provider can own the recovery-codes credential (`updateCredential` returning true, `isConfiguredFor` true). The authenticator is then offered in the browser flow, and rendering its form constructs `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, which does `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get()` and then `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()`. A provider that implements `CredentialInputValidator`/`CredentialInputUpdater` for this type but does not return a fully-formed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (with hashed codes in secretData/credentialData) from `getCredentials` — a perfectly legal, and probably the most common, implementation — causes `NoSuchElementException` or a JSON/NPE inside `createFromCredentialModel`, producing a 500 on the recovery-code login page. The bean should handle an absent/opaque credential (e.g. fall back to not showing a code number) instead of assuming the storage surfaces the full model.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without null check
findings.body: `getCredentials` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user); ... if (myUser.recoveryCodes != null)`. All other methods in this provider (`isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`) guard against `getMyUser` returning null (user removed from the in-memory map while a UserModel/cached entry is still referenced). Here it will throw a NullPointerException from `credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, which is now invoked on every recovery-code login via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`.

findings.title: Test user storage never consumes recovery codes nor supports disabling them, so key behaviours of the new federated path are untested
findings.body: `isValid` for recovery codes only checks `anyMatch(key.equals(challengeResponse))` and never marks the code as used, `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh model from the raw list each call (so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always code 0 and `allCodesUsed()` is never true), and `disableCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` ignore `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`. Consequently `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only covers a single login with code 0 and cannot exercise code consumption, the 'all codes used → CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action' branch in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, re-use of an already used code, or removal of the credential by admin/account REST — exactly the areas where the federated path diverges from the local one.
